slides.teacher_cue: The suffix -ed marks past tense. It has THREE sounds depending on the final sound of the base word. After a voiced sound: -ed = /d/ (played, called, lived). After a voiceless sound: -ed = /t/ (jumped, talked, picked). After /t/ or /d/: -ed = /ɪd/ — a full extra syllable (waited, landed, started, hunted). Rule: if the base ends in /t/ or /d/, you need the extra syllable /ɪd/ to avoid two stops colliding.
slides.expected_response: Students apply the three -ed rules to read and write past tense words correctly.
slides.correction_move: Model all three: played → /d/ (base ends in voiced /d/... wait — played ends in /eɪ/ voiced → /d/). jumped → /t/ (base ends in /p/ voiceless). waited → /ɪd/ (base ends in /t/ — can't add /t/ or /d/ directly). Students sort verbs into three columns.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students adding a full syllable to all -ed words (a common Korean interference — Korean past tense is always an extra syllable).

slides.slide_title: Choose the word where ed says /t/

content_payload.correction_routine: After a voiceless sound, ed says /t/. After a voiced sound, ed says /d/.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Students choose the word where -ed says /t/ and explain what sound comes before the suffix.
slides.expected_response: Students identify jumped as the /t/ example and reject played as /d/.
slides.correction_move: Strip off the suffix and say the base aloud: jump ends in /p/ voiceless, play ends in a voiced sound.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who rely on spelling position rather than final sound of the base word.

slides.slide_title: Choose the word where ed says /ɪd/

content_payload.correction_routine: After /t/ or /d/, ed adds a full syllable: /ɪd/.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both words. Ask students to choose the word with the extra syllable and explain why it happens.
slides.expected_response: Students identify waited as the /ɪd/ example and explain the /t/ base ending.
slides.correction_move: Tap the syllables: wait-ed versus called. Then re-state the t/d rule.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students who make every -ed word two syllables.
